primitives.name: Serve Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: We introduce an outcome metric, serve efficiency, defined as the proportion of first-serve points won within the first three shots of the rally (i.e., serve, return, and the server's next shot).
primitives.latex: E = \frac{\text{Points won on first serve}}{\text{Total first serves}}
primitives.assumptions: Binary outcome assumption; fixed three-shot window; deterministic point resolution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When first serve fails to win point, E = 0.

layer2.mapping: Serve efficiency maps to a probabilistic reward kernel in GSE's action-value function for serve selection.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of first-serve points won per player

primitives.name: First Serve Speed
primitives.verbatim_quote: Open men's singles (2018—2019; 2021—2024), we evaluate how first-serve speed, accuracy, and spatial variation (serve-location entropy) shape point outcomes.
primitives.assumptions: Average speed over all first serves; constant aerodynamic conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Below 10 m/s, serve becomes ineffective due to reduced return pressure.

layer2.mapping: Speed is isomorphic to reaction time compression in GSI’s temporal control model.

primitives.name: Serve Location Entropy
primitives.verbatim_quote: Regression results show that speed has the strongest relationship with serve efficiency, while accuracy in the service box and variation in serve location have smaller but still statistically significant associations.
primitives.assumptions: Uniform distribution of zones; discrete serve locations; normalized probabilities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Entropy approaches zero when all serves land in same zone.

layer2.mapping: Entropy encodes unpredictability in GSE's policy entropy regularization.
layer2.telemetry: Shannon entropy of serve locations per player

The ternary structure of serve effectiveness (speed, accuracy, entropy) forms a vector space where each component contributes additively to a scalar outcome—serve efficiency. Speed acts as a primary driver, compressing returner reaction time and thus increasing likelihood of point win. Accuracy ensures placement within service box, minimizing fault risk. Entropy introduces stochasticity, reducing predictability and enhancing strategic value. These primitives form a dual basis in GSI’s Bayesian framework: speed and accuracy are deterministic features, while entropy is a probabilistic feature. In GSE, they define a Markovian state transition from serve initiation to rally outcome, where each primitive modifies the belief state over return pressure and tactical options. Failure modes include over-reliance on speed alone (reducing entropy), or neglecting accuracy (leading to faults). Multicollinearity is mitigated through standardized regression coefficients and empirical correlation matrices showing weak interdependencies among components.
